name: Thessaly Oduya-Varga
role: Senior Project Manager, Tessera Infrastructure Division
location: Grand Corridor, Tessera Infrastructure Hub — open-plan office, desk seven
description:
Thessaly has the kind of face that reads as permanently slightly amused, which is either accurate or a very effective mask depending on the day. They are medium height, compact, with light brown skin and the kind of effortlessly symmetrical features that suggest either genetics or a very good cosmetic package — in fact it's genetics, a fact they find privately funny. Their hair is color-shifting, cycling slowly through dark blues and greens during work hours and switching to a deep amber setting they call 'off-duty mode.' They dress practically: clean lines, nothing that catches on equipment, a jacket with actual pockets. A small silver ring through their left nostril is their only visible jewelry.

Thessaly is someone who keeps everything moving — projects, people, conversations, agendas. They have an almost physical intolerance for stagnation and an ability to hold seventeen interdependent variables in their head without apparent effort. They're not charismatic in the conventional sense: they don't perform warmth. But they're fair, they remember everything, and they're reliably the calmest person in any crisis, which generates a particular kind of loyalty in the people who work under them. They grew up in a Tier 3 household in Shorewood Terrace with two working parents who modeled relentless competence, and they absorbed it completely.

core_fears: A project failure so public it dismantles the professional identity they've spent fifteen years building
Being genuinely needed by someone and not being able to deliver
core_desires: To build things that last past the quarterly cycle
To have one relationship — professional or personal — where they don't feel like the only reliable person in the room
coping_mechanisms: Physical exercise — specifically swimming, alone, no audience
blind_spots: Mistakes efficiency for care — sometimes solves problems people needed to feel heard about first
Underestimates how exhausting their baseline competence level is for people around them
psychology.secret: Tessera's current flagship civic integration project — a Ferrogate transit expansion through the Grand Corridor — is running on falsified cost projections that Thessaly didn't create but signed off on under pressure from a divisional VP. The numbers will not survive contact with year-two actuals. They've been quietly preparing a paper trail that positions the VP as solely responsible, which is mostly but not entirely true.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Project management vernacular used precisely, not as filler. Comfortable with technical vocabulary across multiple domains. Informal in private, formal in meetings — a switch they flip visibly and without apology.
speech_patterns.cadence: Brisk but not rushed. Doesn't repeat themselves. Phrases things as decisions, not suggestions.
verbal_tics: 'Right, so—' to open any substantive statement
'That's a separate conversation' to table things they don't have time for
example_lines: 'The timeline is aggressive. It's also what we agreed to. If you have a new constraint, give me the data and I'll reassess — otherwise we execute on current.'
'I'm not unsympathetic. I'm also holding four other workstreams right now, so tell me what you actually need.'

story_hooks: The falsified cost projections on the transit expansion are starting to attract outside scrutiny — a Ferrogate Transit internal auditor has been asking questions, and Thessaly needs to decide whether to come clean, accelerate the blame-shift, or find a third option.
A worker on one of their construction sub-sites goes missing under circumstances that a site foreman is trying very hard to keep off the official incident report.
narrative_function: Organizational hub who knows where bodies are buried administratively; quest giver for logistics problems; can provide access or obstacle depending on relationship; grounded, reliable voice of pragmatic institutional knowledge.
augmentations: Color-shifting hair mod (blues, greens, amber — self-curated palette). Cortical memory-assist implant for project data retention. Mild haptic feedback overlay in both hands for interface work. No cosmetic eye mods — they specifically declined them, no explanation given.
daily_life: In at 07:30, runs three parallel project status meetings before noon, eats lunch at their desk while doing vendor correspondence, spends afternoons on site visits or stakeholder calls, leaves by 19:00 unless something is actively on fire. Has a Ferrogate Transit season pass and reads physical books on the commute — an affectation they're unapologetic about.

decision_rules: Gather information before acting, but set a hard deadline for the information-gathering phase
Protect the team first, protect the project second, protect yourself third — except when the third is unavoidable
Never make a promise you don't intend to keep; it destroys the only currency that matters
escalation_ladder: Address the problem directly and privately
Escalate with documentation to the appropriate authority
If institutional channels fail, construct a defensive paper trail and proceed unilaterally

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Cordial, efficient, assessing — gives people one chance to demonstrate they're worth further investment
interpersonal_modes.friends: Dry, loyal, occasionally unexpectedly tender in a way that surprises both parties

stress_responses.low: Tightens their planning documents, adds more contingency lines
stress_responses.medium: Becomes more directive in speech, less consultative
stress_responses.high: Goes completely quiet, disappears into solo work for several hours, emerges with a restructured plan

contradictions: Champions institutional accountability while constructing a private cover-your-ass paper trail they're not proud of
habits: Updates their personal project journal every evening before leaving the office — a habit kept since their first placement
Leaves a data offering at the Grand Corridor E.L.F. shrine on the first of every month — always efficiency metrics from completed projects, 'as proof of work'
breaking_points: If the falsified projections result in harm to transit workers or residents rather than just budget overruns, they will not be able to contain it

timeline.event: Joins Tessera Infrastructure Division as junior coordinator
Promoted to Project Manager after successful completion of Kenwood Gate grid upgrade
Promoted to Senior Project Manager, Civic Integration Projects
Signs off on falsified cost projections for Grand Corridor transit expansion under VP pressure
